findings.title: Keyboard focus is lost when the selected tile scrolls out of view; arrow keys then leave the grid instead of navigating
findings.evidence: Probe P6r (synthetic-probe-r2-result-20261016T115150.json), real headless key routing: without scrolling, Right moves selection 3 to 4. After scrolling the grid to offset 3063, the selected container (index 3) is no longer realized and focus is null. A routed Right then leaves the selection at 3 and the offset unchanged, and moves focus to a TextBox in the connection row (typing would edit it). Probe P6 (key raised directly on the ListBox): selection jumps to index 0. Baseline P6r (main fa259f2 LibraryView, VirtualizingStackPanel): focus stays on the ListBoxItem, and Down moves 3 to 4 and scrolls back (offset 2639 to 204). Code: MeasureOverride removes every realized index outside the viewport, including the focused container (LibraryTilePanel.cs:43); GetControl resolves the origin only from realized containers (102-118). Avalonia VirtualizingStackPanel keeps the focused element realized for this reason. The grid-keyboard contract never scrolls away (RommDesktopBehaviorContracts.cs:184-192).
findings.rationale: The correction slice promised normal ListBox keyboard semantics alongside off-screen detachment (record lines 90-91), and the parent claims keyboard support. A routine mouse-wheel scroll followed by an arrow key either sends focus to an unrelated input or (when the ListBox gets the key) resets selection to the first tile. This is a regression against main and a sibling of the container-lifecycle change, and no test detects it.
findings.correction: Write the test first: select a tile, scroll it out of view, press a routed arrow key, and assert focus stays in the grid with selection moving relative to the selected tile. Then retain the focused (KeyboardNavigation tab-once-active) container when it leaves the viewport (park it, as VirtualizingStackPanel does), or re-establish focus and origin from the selected index, without weakening the off-screen cover cancellation that P1b proves.

Tile slot versus content: a realized ListBoxItem needs 146x177 against the fixed 136x174 slot (Fluent padding 12,9,12,12). The overflow is absorbed by item padding, with no container overlap (P10). Cosmetic; deriving the slot from the template would remove it.

ListsView now reloads the selected collection members on every rail refresh (selection cleared by ItemsSource replacement, then re-selected), adding GetRomAsync traffic per refresh. SelectCollectionAsync can miss navigation if a rail refresh is already in flight (_refreshingRail early return); not reproduced. Shared and visible selection stay equal either way, so Delete safety holds.
Pre-existing, not introduced: ListsView Create, Delete and Refresh handlers have no exception capture (as in main).
